描述_ZN: Portrait of King Zhu Youxiang of Xing, Ming, on silk with color, 108.3 cm in length and 76 cm in width.　　The painting is unsigned and must have been made by a court painter. The figure in the painting is taken as a frontal portrait, outlined in line and then painted in color, without haloing the facial features, and the costume focuses on highlighting canonical features, with clear patterns, detached from the folds of the clothing. The whole work is flat and vivid, with more expression of the form than of the figures, making it slightly dull and rigid.　　Zhu Youxiang (1476-1519), the fourth son of Emperor Chenghua of Ming Dynasty, was born to Chen Fei Shao. He was crowned King of Xing in the twenty-third year of Ming Chenghua (1487) and died on June 17, 1519, at the age of 44, posthumously as King Xian. In 1521, when Wuzong died without an heir, Zhu Houchong, a cousin of Wuzong and son of Yu Yu, succeeded to the throne as Emperor Jiajing. The Jiajing Emperor posthumously honored his biological father, Yu Yu, as "Emperor Xingxian".　　The picture shows Zhu Youxiang dressed in Ming imperial costume; this picture is probably not a portrait of him during his lifetime, but from the Jiajing years onwards.
